Cutoff-consistent evidence is more consistent with a recent downside reversal and failed near-term transmission than with confirmed broad continuation: 24h/72h prices, ETH-relative performance, proxy breadth, sentiment and several spot microstructure readings weakened. The signal is uneven—BTC's 4h return and 12h aggressive flow were positive, open interest fell between owner captures, and rotation gauges remain between published thresholds. No distribution or exit signal is established. The post-cutoff breadth and forensics observations are excluded from the contemporaneous basis; the 1h API horizon has zero actual span and is not treated as a return. This shadow interpretation does not resolve either late-cycle failure mode: exiting too early could forgo remaining upside, while persistent deterioration could make a late response costly.
uncertainties: The 1h API observation has zero actual span; the nominal 4h, 12h, 24h and 72h windows span 3, 11, 23 and 71 hours, respectively.
Breadth is a point-in-time filtered top-100 proxy with changing membership and rolling-24h semantics; canonical broad-alt and large-cap breadth remain unconfirmed.
The latest settled ETF figures are for 2026-10-07 and do not establish the direction of subsequent sessions.
BTC dominance is present as a settled 2026-10-07 CMC observation, but a comparable current change is not supplied.
Macro owner was disabled in the latest capture; current macro observations are unavailable there. Earlier macro values are not assumed current.

The after-cutoff rich-breadth and pullback-forensics captures cannot be aligned to the stated decision cutoff; liquidation data also report lower bounds with unverified completeness and fragile legacy REST sourcing.
Funding and open-interest comparisons cover only the interval between captures; they do not establish a sustained leverage regime.
Action Compass cohorts are descriptive, LOW-quality calibration samples and do not define pullback, distribution, exit, re-entry or timing rules.
Forecast candidates are unratified research objects, not canonical forecasts or portfolio actions.
